facts.statement: K3 SoC integrates 8 X100 general-purpose cores and 8 A100 AI cores (2 A100 clusters, 60 TOPS aggregate AI compute) using RISC-V homogeneous fusion: scalar (standard ISA), vector (RVV 1.0) and matrix (IME extension) compute share one RISC-V programming model, and standard Linux threads drive AI computation without a heterogeneous scheduler or driver management.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/432da714bd719f3506e3fb28b39f1f35fa1a8f54702382d66e010ec92acb30f6/root_overview.md.search.txt:12-14; docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/83ddde6d173d633a2b89bad966f7ec23ae7ab4699185cf85989521a79c03d066/concept.md.search.txt:11-22 (4.1.1); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:181-183

facts.statement: A100 execution resources (Preview 2026-01-29 description, to be reconciled with production hardware at board porting): each of the 2 A100 clusters comprises 4 scalar cores, 2 vector cores, 2 local-memory banks and a shared L2; the Tensor Core (IME-2.0, 1024/2048-bit datapath) is shared by two compute cores and accepts one MMA instruction per cycle from each; a per-core private IME-1.0 unit (256/512-bit, INT8xINT8->INT32 small MAC) also exists; each core has an independent 512-bit load channel and the front end dual-issues one 512-bit load plus one MMA per cycle.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:680-685,717-745 (3.2/3.2.2)

facts.statement: Execution-model policy for this compiler: parallelize one operator across native workers and vectorize within each worker; work may be repartitioned from the source grid when semantics permit; a persistent worker pool receives native work ranges and threads/workspaces are reused across calls; cross-worker dependencies use explicit stages, synchronization and merges; coverage, tails, ownership, visibility and repeated execution must be validated at 1/2/4/8 workers, and representative multi-worker cases must distribute useful work.
facts.source: chip.md#3-execution-model (POLICY, lines 63-70)

facts.statement: Measured scheduling model under the declared QEMU endpoint: a persistent pthread pool executes work ranges with distinct guest tids at 1/2/4/8 threads (full 32771-item coverage, one pool initialization, warmup run included) - the scheduling unit is the OS-scheduled Linux thread; a worker count of one is the single-thread serial configuration. QEMU guest threads are not physical A100 cores (assumption A001).
facts.source: probe: TOOLCHAIN_PROBES.json threads rows (persistent_pool_two_stages, qemu-functional, passed=true at 1/2/4/8); docs/compiler-agent/ENVIRONMENT.md Multi-worker execution/observation

facts.statement: Vendor-stack scheduling reference (not this project's codegen contract): the official X100 runtime dispatches tile-level compute tasks onto A100-cluster thread groups - one A100 cluster maps to a group of four A100 Linux threads, two clusters form two groups totalling eight A100 Linux threads, dispatched least-loaded; official inference examples assign AI core IDs 8-15 explicitly (SPACEMIT_PERFER_CORE_ID=8,9,10,11 / 12,13,14,15) and K3 provides 8 AI cores supporting up to 8-thread inference. These are documented examples; the actual allowed core set must be probed on the board.

facts.statement: Board address spaces (K3 main CPU domain map): RISCV TCM 64MB at 0x0000_0000; DDR DRAM 64GB at 0x1_0000_0000; 128KB boot-ROM; 512KB SRAM shared by Main CPU and Real CPU domains; hardware Spinlock (32 units, 1KB window) at 0xCAC9_1C00; Mailbox0-6; AIDMA_0-7, DMA350_0-1 and HSDMA controllers. RCPU domain additionally maps its own SRAM view.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/4f7d0d5c4e77c7a0647e946a698656682ead8a9ae7fbc9fae6a83da37e625c6e/06_address_map.md.search.txt:15-17,55-62,167-177,200; docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/555a9e44f2b4ac508251fc459abd2f3356e21469e346a430295c0223af9c2007/09_memory_storage.md.search.txt:9-13 (9.1 On-Chip Memory)

facts.statement: A100 per-cluster memory hierarchy: 32KB L1 I-cache and 32KB L1 D-cache per core; 1MB L2 cache per cluster; 1.5MB scratchpad per cluster; L1 D-cache supports MESI and L2 supports MOESI coherence. The L2 and the 1.5MB scratchpad are cluster-shared resources, not per-thread private capacity.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/ff2340c355516e190769949abbfe57d2121efbe72326b5fc65b166f6cd55d90d/08_cpu.md.search.txt:54-59 (8.2.2); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/69a7cd5b8836085506f53f1b02ad8aa624790eb23ca573ca584e226ee1246358/k3_ds.md.search.txt:147-153

facts.statement: Per-hart local storage: each A100 hart has a private vector register file of 32 vector registers x 128B = 4KB at VLEN=1024, which the architecture Preview describes as an effective 4KB ultra-fast local scratchpad for locality optimizations (e.g. holding a broadcast Scale vector or a FlashAttention accumulation in registers).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:727-731 (3.2.1),1261-1267 (5.2.2)

facts.statement: The A100 dataflow design (Preview) uses software-managed local memory and decoupled access-execute operation - asynchronous DMA prefetch overlapping memory movement with computation; the K3 DMA controller is a 16-channel flow-through engine (memory-to-memory/peripheral, burst 8/16/32/64B, up to 8191 bytes per descriptor with chaining, 64-bit addressing above 4GB). The software interfaces for TCM/DMA allocation, completion, visibility and lifetime are not specified in the pack and remain unverified (assumption A00x).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:666-672 (3.2 dataflow axes); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/e3c328de09ccec8594134bfa2d29c635b7cc78578dde2cfe28de169983b9ecb7/dma.md.search.txt:7-42 (16.1.1-16.1.2)

facts.statement: A100 ISA baseline: fully compliant with the RISC-V RVA23* standard (RVA23U64 user + RVA23S64 supervisor) EXCLUDING the Hypervisor extension; SV39 virtual memory; 32 PMP entries; integrated PMU; ACLINT + APLIC interrupt controllers (AIA). Optional extensions listed: vector crypto zvkng/zvksg, plus zvbc, zfh, zbc, zvfh, zfbfmin, zvfbfmin, zvfbfwma, sdtri, svvptc, sspm, smepmp, smstateen, smcntrpmf. RVA23U64 makes V (vector) mandatory together with Zvfhmin/Zvbb/Zvkt.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/ff2340c355516e190769949abbfe57d2121efbe72326b5fc65b166f6cd55d90d/08_cpu.md.search.txt:53-76 (8.2.2 incl. facts.statement: A100 vector extension: RVV 1.0 with VLEN=1024; the Vector Unit is driven by two parallel vector pipelines performing instruction splitting, dependency handling and vector register-file reads/writes; operators are classified INT, FP, CRYPTO, FDV and IME-1.0 by instruction type and datapath; the register file provides 32 architectural vector registers v0-v31 of 128B each.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/ff2340c355516e190769949abbfe57d2121efbe72326b5fc65b166f6cd55d90d/08_cpu.md.search.txt:60 (8.2.2); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:729-760 (3.2.1)

facts.statement: SpacemiT IME instruction set (Zvvm_spacemit profile, version 0.6 public release 2026-04-13): 46 custom AI instructions, all prefixed smt. (SMT vendor prefix); it reuses the 32 RVV vector registers for 2D matrix tiles with no dedicated matrix register file (no extra architectural state or context-switch overhead). The A100 core in K3 supports 13 sub-extensions: Xsmti4i32mm, Xsmti8i32mm, Xsmti8i32mm_slide, Xsmti4i32mm_42sp, Xsmti8i32mm_42sp, Xsmti4fp16mm_scl16f, Xsmti4bf16mm_scl16f, Xsmti8fp16mm_scl16f, Xsmti8bf16mm_scl16f, Xsmtfp16fp32mm, Xsmtbf16fp32mm, Xsmtfp16fp32mm_slide, Xsmtbf16fp32mm_slide; the toolchain names the A100 set collectively Xsmtvdotii. Chinese and English v0.6 editions in the pack agree.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:5-9,56,206-243 (1.6/1.7),2333-2339 (App. B); cross-checked with the Chinese edition docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/efb5d87ac66581c12a931698b95db2ae840a57110cf23e429142fca07662e189/ime_extension.md.search.txt:91-144

facts.statement: A100 IME tile shapes and implementation parameters (LMUL=1 tiles): INT4 x INT4 -> INT32 tile 8x32x8; INT8 x INT8 -> INT32 tile 8x16x8 (integer family: lambda=4, MUL_C=2, SEW=32); FP16/BF16 x FP16/BF16 -> FP32 tile 8x8x8 (MUL_C=2, SEW=32); 4:2 structured sparse: INT4 8x64x8, INT8 8x32x8; block-scaled integer (Int4/Int8 + FP16/BF16 scale -> FP16/BF16): lambda=8, MUL_C=1, SEW=16, tiles 8x32x8 (Int4) / 8x16x8 (Int8); sliding-window variants keep their base family tile. lambda is fixed per instruction family and NOT configurable via vtype; MUL_C = VLEN/(SEW x lambda^2).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:274-317 (2.1.2),371-396 (2.5),2313-2329 (App. A)

facts.statement: IME operand and data-layout contract: vs1 holds tile A (row-major), vs2 holds tile B (column-major); B^T in the semantics C <- C + A x B^T is a geometric layout statement and does NOT require a software transpose of B; vd holds both the initial accumulator and the result with an implementation-defined result layout; Int4 inputs use packed nibble storage (element 2n in bits [3:0], 2n+1 in bits [7:4] of byte n); EEW=8/16 use standard linear vector element ordering; integer signedness variants (none/u/us/su) select signed/unsigned interpretation of A and B with the accumulator always signed.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:67-86 (1.4),144-155 (1.5),437-479 (2.7),529-538 (4.2)

facts.statement: Negative ISA facts - absent operations in the SpacemiT matrix extension: community Zvvm instructions vmmacc, vwmmacc, vfmmacc, vfqwmmacc and vf8wmmacc are NOT supported (functional equivalents: vqwmmacc->smt.vmadot* Int8, v8wmmacc->smt.vmadot* Int4, vfwmmacc->smt.vfwmadot, vfwimmacc->smt.vmadot.hp* Int8+scale, vfqwimmacc->smt.vmadot.hp* Int4+scale; vf8wimmacc e5m2 scale not supported); the Zvvmtls dedicated matrix load/store extension is NOT implemented (similar functionality via smt.vpack); mixed FP16/BF16 input formats within one instruction are NOT defined; the standard RVV vm mask bit is NOT used as a mask control for matrix multiplication instructions (no vector-mask semantics defined for this instruction class); Zvvm vtype.lambda / vtype.altfmt_A/B / vtype.altfmt CSR fields are not implemented (A100 uses MCPM instead).
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:329-346 (2.3),489-513 (Ch.3 differences table),1397-1404 (6.1.3)

facts.statement: IME illegal conditions (refusal/trap contract): LMUL != 1 in any IME instruction raises an illegal instruction exception (all other LMUL encodings reserved); when MUL_C=2 the destination vd must be even-numbered (vd and vd+1 form the group) and the destination group must not overlap vs1 or vs2; sliding-window instructions additionally require vs1 even-numbered; sparse instructions use v0/v1 as recovery masks with imm2 segment select; scale instructions use v0/v1 as scale parameter registers with imm3 group select; for smt.vfwmadot* the floating-point input format must match the MCPM.BF16 setting, else illegal.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:104-129 (1.5),329-352 (2.3),398-435 (2.6),670-675 (5.1.4),1424-1429 (6.1.5)

facts.statement: IME data-layout transformation instructions: smt.vpack.vv, smt.vupack.vv, smt.vnpack.vv, smt.vnspack.vv, smt.vnpack4.vv, smt.vnspack4.vv (functionally equivalent to Zvzip vzip.vv / vunzipe.v / vunzipo.v / vpaire.vv / vpairo.v); imm2 selects interleave granularity (SEW/128/256/512-bit for pack/upack; 32/64/128/256-bit for the narrowing forms); vd must be even-numbered for vpack/vupack; bit [14] distinguishes normal vs saturating narrowing; encoding uses the 0101011 opcode with vd[4:1] packing where the even-register constraint frees bit 0.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/bd69e01a6280ae5ab4493ea82b0e819fb34f093da43c264fc3be3c6291a8c6c8/ime_extension.md.search.txt:509-513 (Ch.3),585-592 (4.3),2255-2311 (8.6)

facts.statement: FP8 and headline compute specifications (Preview 2026-01-29; not probed, not a performance target under correctness_only): A100 integrates customized FP8 (E4M3 and E5M2) vector conversion instructions and FP8 operands are converted to BF16 before computation; headline K3 AI compute: INT4 30 dense / 60 sparse TOPS with block scaling, INT8 15 dense / 30 sparse, BF16/FP16 7.5 (IEEE FP16 and bfloat16 formats), FP8 7.5. The development corpus excludes fp8, so FP8 is not on the current input path.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/9564d4ba5ed9a64d71c0c7e5bf0c8f7d74ed717fd0aa71265328f8c1eaea8c91/K3_architecture_preview.pdf.search.txt:158-165 (Table 1),970-985 (FP8 conversion instructions); corpus exclusion: ops/README.md (declared subset: no fp8)

facts.statement: Input corpus dtype surface that binds the ISA families on the input path: 500 operators / 2734 cases with dtypes bfloat16, bool, float16, float32, int16, int32, int64, int8 only; the declared subset is forward-only inference: no gradient kernels, no fp8, no input_precision=/allow_tf32= (fp32 tl.dot is IEEE, pinned by TRITON_F32_DEFAULT=ieee in the runner); bf16 is the primary perf-lane dtype. Consequently the applicable IME families for the input path are INT8 8x16x8 and FP16/BF16 8x8x8 (the BF16 family currently blocked by the emulator gap), with int4/sparse/scale families available on hardware but not exercised by corpus dtypes.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/CORPUS_LOCK.json (500 operators, 2734 cases, dtypes bfloat16/bool/float16/float32/int16/int32/int64/int8); ops/README.md (declared subset); chip.md#4 (input and numeric contract)

facts.statement: Other-chip and cross-generation exclusions: the K1 chip (4 X60 + 4 A60 cores, A60 VLEN=256, native matrix tile 4x8x4, 0.5 TOPS/core INT8, cpufp measurements ~511 GOPS IME / ~66 GFLOPS fp16 vfma per A60 core) is a different generation and its figures and tile shapes do NOT extend to A100; the X100 core in the same K3 SoC has RVV 1.0 VLEN=256 (not 1024) and 4MB L2 per cluster - generated computation targets A100 cores only, never X100 or RT24. chip.md states that other-chip examples, earlier matrix proposals and performance chapters do not expand this project's requirements.
facts.source: docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/462bf27aed1712f9ca43fee5cb6302de444e4e1c66f513a08be5a8bd62b445a1/instruction.md.search.txt:26-33 (K1/A60); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/83ddde6d173d633a2b89bad966f7ec23ae7ab4699185cf85989521a79c03d066/concept.md.search.txt:26-56 (K1 figures); docs/compiler-agent/target-material/sources/ff2340c355516e190769949abbfe57d2121efbe72326b5fc65b166f6cd55d90d/08_cpu.md.search.txt:22 (X100 VLEN=256); chip.md:114-116 (pack scope note)

facts.statement: Register model: 32 general-purpose registers (RISC-V standard) plus 32 architectural vector registers v0-v31 at 128B each (VLEN=1024) per A100 hart; v0 serves the standard RVV mask-register role; the vector register file is per-core private; the IME reuses exactly these vector registers for matrix tiles with no additional architectural state, so matrix context switching carries no cost beyond ordinary RVV state.
